description:
Close the origin so ONLY Cloudflare can reach it, then MEASURE that it worked.

    method='nginx'    one file in nginx's `http` context
                      (/etc/nginx/conf.d/00-cloudflare-only.conf), so it covers EVERY vhost
                      at once without touching a single site file, and needs no cloud
                      permissions. Also installs a log_format that keeps the true visitor
                      address in the logs.
    method='firewall' the packet-level nft allowlist (SSH/loopback/established always
                      permitted, daily range refresh).
    method='both'     default, defence in depth.

    Cloudflare's ranges are FETCHED at the moment of use, never hardcoded. If the fetch
    fails or comes back suspiciously short the tool REFUSES - a partial allowlist takes
    every site on the box down at once.

    It will NOT enable the real_ip module, and it REFUSES to apply on a box that already has
    `set_real_ip_from` / `real_ip_header`: real_ip rewrites $remote_addr and allow/deny reads
    that SAME variable, so the allowlist would start matching the visitor's address and 403
    everybody (this cost a client two minutes of downtime). Pass disable_real_ip=true to
    comment those directives out - the log format installed here already carries the true
    client address, so nothing is lost.

    Verified end to end: nginx -t, reload, a loopback request must still be served, and the
    origin is probed from THIS machine before and after. If Cloudflare stops serving, the
    change is rolled back automatically. `verify=true` (default) therefore REQUIRES domain +
    origin_ip - the tool will not claim an origin is closed without measuring it.

    After this, banning IPs on the box stops working for web traffic - see `consequence`.
    `revert=True` reopens the origin. dry_run shows everything; confirm applies.
name: origin_lock
